applicable_failures: The agent's stated goal was to enumerate all 117 candidates. It then screened them by a filename regex (lpa|limited|partnership|fund|side|subscription|key|claw|capital|operating|formation|investor|agreement) and says it will read only the plausible fund-formation matters. The first run of that screen failed with a SyntaxError. The rerun wrote its output to /tmp/candidate_relevant_names.txt, which holds 101 lines for 117 candidates, so about 16 matters matched no filename. Those 16 are dropped silently.

The shown output is for 1001-00002, which looks like a GP/ManCo restructuring with an LPA amendment rather than a fund formation. The 'plausible fund-formation' subset is hand-picked from filenames, and matters such as 1001-00002 through 1021-00001 (the 60 listed with no folder opened) risk never being opened.
critique.concerns: The listing itself worked: 117 matters and 6,133 lines were written to a file. But the output was never reviewed, so the agent has seen only a truncated slice. The filename regex is broad but still misses documents with unusual names, and key-person or clawback terms usually sit inside the LPA text rather than in a filename. Shrinking the set by filename before any text check repeats the known failure. The 60 matters flagged as having no folder opened remain unexamined.
critique.recommendation: Keep all 117 candidates in play. List the 16 matters with no filename hit and review their file lists manually. Then run a text scan for key-person and clawback terms across every candidate matter's documents, with no filename prefilter, and print only per-matter hit counts. Read the governing LPA and side documents for every matter that hits.
